name: Assessment, Observations & Deterioration
pathways: assessment → observation → clinical concern → escalation → acknowledgement → acceptance → reassessment → resolution.
rules: Record every observation set as a discrete, timestamped, additive event linked to a calculated early-warning score; a new set never overwrites or replaces a prior one.

Distinguish a scheduled observation (due per rostered frequency) from an unscheduled, concern-triggered observation, and record a missed-scheduled-observation as its own fact rather than leaving a silent gap.

Where a calculated score crosses a locally defined threshold, automatically create a linked Deterioration Event and Escalation record; the system flags that a response is required and by when, and does not determine what that response should be.

name: Medication
pathways: proposed → ordered/prescribed → verified/reviewed → supplied/dispensed → scheduled → administered/taken → monitored → modified → held → resumed → ceased → reconciled → historical.
rules: Changing a dose, route, or frequency creates a new linked version rather than overwriting the prior one — what was actually prescribed at a given time must stay reconstructable.

name: Administration Event
pathways: due/scheduled where applicable → prepared → required checks → administered OR refused OR withheld OR omitted OR unavailable OR delayed → monitoring/reassessment where required → completed.
rules: Recording an administration event requires the recording worker to confirm patient identity, medication identity, dose, route and time against the current order at the point of administration; the system presents the check, it does not perform it.

Where a medication is locally defined as high-risk and requiring independent double-check, the event captures the second checker's identity separately from the administering worker — one worker cannot fill both roles.

name: Consent / Authority
rules: Record the person's information, choice, consent/refusal/withdrawal and supporting evidence as distinct states; the software must not decide competence or validity.

name: Escalation
pathways: trigger → escalation requirement → responsible recipient → escalation initiated → received → acknowledged → response/action → reassessment → resolved/further escalation.
rules: An Escalation record captures who was notified, by what means, at what time, and their acknowledged response, as distinct fields; 'notified' and 'acknowledged' are never collapsed into a single state.
Where a defined response time elapses without acknowledgement, the escalation surfaces as unresolved and remains visible rather than silently expiring.

name: Observation / Measurement
rules: One observation record holds exactly one measurement type, one value, one time and one recorder; a set taken together (e.g. a full vital-signs round) links via a shared set/episode identifier rather than merging into a single free-text entry.
An amended reading preserves the original as a superseded version with reason and author; it is never silently overwritten.

name: Assessment

name: Diagnosis / Problem
pathways: suspected/provisional → confirmed where appropriate → active → resolved/inactive; history retained.

name: Engine / Configuration / Object Test
pathways: Yes → consider Clinical Engine.
Yes → Shared Lifecycle Object.
Yes → Service Configuration.
Yes → Cross-System / Governance Capability.
Yes → redesign it.

name: Allergy, Intolerance & Adverse Reaction
pathways: reported reaction → source/provenance → substance/product identification → reaction evidence → severity/context → clinical assessment → classification → confirmed OR suspected OR refuted OR uncertain → active safety state → review → amendment/resolution where clinically appropriate.
rules: A recorded allergy or adverse reaction is checked automatically at prescribing and at administration; a match presents a block or warning per local policy, but proceeding or not remains a recorded human decision.
No allergy or adverse-reaction entry is deleted outright; correcting one made in error creates a superseding record with a reason, preserving the original for audit.

name: Clinical Risk / Safety Flag
pathways: underlying risk identified → assessment → safety flag generated where warranted → visible in appropriate contexts → review → changed/ceased.
rules: A safety flag (falls risk, allergy, wandering/confusion risk, infection precaution, etc.) must be visible at the point of any relevant workflow — medication administration, transfer, discharge — without the worker navigating away from their current task.
Flags are versioned and never silently deleted; removing or downgrading one requires a recorded reason and the authority that made the change.

name: Isolation / Transmission Precaution
pathways: transmission concern → IPC assessment → precaution requirement → precaution type → implementation → location/environmental requirements → review → modification → cessation.

name: Clinical Goal
pathways: need/problem → goal proposed → agreed/authorised where appropriate → target/timeframe → interventions linked → progress → reassessment → achieved OR partially achieved OR not achieved OR changed OR ceased.

name: Clinical Outcome
pathways: baseline → target → measurement → achieved/not achieved/partial/unknown → review.

name: Clinical Decision
pathways: decision required → available evidence → options considered → risks/benefits/context → patient preference where applicable → authorised decision-maker → decision → implementation requirements → review/reconsideration.

name: Multidisciplinary Team / Case Conference
pathways: conference/review required → participants → relevant canonical evidence referenced → discussion → decisions → actions → responsible people/services → due dates → follow-up.

name: Clinical Consultation
pathways: consultation requested → received → accepted/declined → clinician reviews available evidence → assessment/contact where required → advice/recommendation → requesting team receives advice → actions → consultation closed.

name: Clinical Review / Reassessment
pathways: review due/triggered → current evidence obtained → previous state referenced → new assessment → comparison → decision → actions → next review requirement.

name: Monitoring Plan
pathways: monitoring requirement → parameter → method → frequency/timing → threshold/target → responsible person/team → monitoring event → result → review → action → continuation/modification/cessation.

name: Clinical Restriction / Precaution
pathways: clinical need identified → authorised restriction → parameters → effective time → communication → implementation → review → modification/cessation.

name: Nutrition / Diet Order
pathways: nutrition/swallowing requirement → assessment → authorised diet/nutrition state → preparation/provision → delivery → intake → tolerance → monitoring → review → modification/cessation.

name: Blood / Biological Product
pathways: clinical requirement → request → compatibility/suitability → product allocation → issue → receipt → bedside identity/product verification → commencement → administration → monitoring → completion → reaction/outcome → traceability closure.

name: Clinical Equipment
pathways: equipment identity → availability → allocation → patient/service use reference → setup → safety check → use → fault/problem → withdrawal/quarantine → maintenance/repair → return to service → retirement.

name: Location / Bed / Care Space
pathways: location requirement → placement request → location/bed allocated → patient movement → arrival → occupied/current location → movement/transfer → vacated.

name: Leave / Temporary Absence
pathways: leave considered/requested → clinical/legal authority where applicable → leave conditions → authorised → departure → current absence → expected return → return OR failure/delay to return → reassessment.

name: Patient Preference
pathways: preference expressed → context/source → current relevance → acknowledged → incorporated where possible → reviewed/changed/withdrawn.

name: Advance-Care Information
pathways: discussion → preference/information → formal directive/decision where legally applicable → review/change → current status with history.

name: Decision-Making Capacity Assessment
pathways: decision requiring assessment → reason for concern → relevant functional assessment → communication/support measures → determination within applicable professional/legal framework → decision/context covered → time → reassessment requirement.

name: Whānau / Family / Support-Person Involvement
pathways: person identity → relationship → patient preference → involvement requested/permitted → information-sharing authority → decision-making authority where independently established → communication events → changes/restrictions.

name: Interpreter / Communication Accessibility Requirement
pathways: need identified → requirement recorded → service arrangement → interpreter/support booked → provided → outcome → continuing requirement reviewed.

name: External / Imported Clinical Information
pathways: external information received → patient matching → source identified → integrity/provenance retained → authorised availability → clinical review → incorporated/referenced where appropriate → amendment/update from source where applicable.

name: Clinical Coding / Classification
pathways: source clinical information → coding requirement → code assignment → validation → finalised coding → amendment where appropriate.

name: Patient-Reported Information
pathways: patient report → source/time/context → structured or narrative information → clinical review where applicable → incorporated into assessment/decision where appropriate → updated/corrected by source.

name: Questionnaire / Assessment Instrument
pathways: instrument required/offered → version identified → administered → responses → score/result → interpretation → clinical action where applicable → repeat assessment.

name: Clinical Image / Media
pathways: order/purpose → capture/import → patient/context validation → store → interpretation/use → retention/access.

name: Fluid Balance / Intake and Output
pathways: intake/output event → running balance → review → period close → next period.

name: Patient Weight / Height / Growth State
pathways: measurement → validation → longitudinal state → trend/growth interpretation → clinical action where indicated.

name: Functional Status
pathways: baseline → current assessment → assistance requirement → intervention → reassessment → changed/current state.

name: Baseline / Usual State
pathways: usual state → current difference → action → outcome

name: Clinical Episode
pathways: initiated → active → encounters/events accumulate → transition → closed → reopened/new episode only according to defined rules.

name: Named Clinician / Team Assignment
pathways: assignment required → proposed → confirmed → active → changed/covered → ended.

name: Patient Allocation
pathways: patient requires care → staffing/team context → proposed allocation → senior/authorised review → confirmed allocation → active assignment → change/reallocation → handover/end.

name: Clinical Status / Acuity
pathways: clinical evidence → acuity assessment/calculation → current status → escalation/resource implications → reassessment → changed status.

name: Deterioration Event
pathways: change detected → evidence → concern/trigger → escalation → clinical response → intervention → reassessment → outcome → further escalation/closure.
rules: A Deterioration Event may be created automatically (score-triggered) or manually (worker concern regardless of score); the two trigger types remain distinguishable in the record, since a below-threshold worker concern is itself safety-relevant data.
Creating a Deterioration Event mandates a linked Escalation record. The event cannot be closed without a recorded human review and, where applicable, its escalation outcome.

name: Incident / Adverse Clinical Event
pathways: event/concern → immediate clinical response → incident notification where required → safety review → investigation linkage → findings → actions → closure.
rules: An incident record — including a near-miss, such as a wrong dose caught before administration — is created as its own event, separate from and never overwriting the clinical record it relates to; prevented harm is captured with the same rigour as harm that occurred.

name: Death Event
pathways: death occurs/identified → verification → certification references → notifications → clinical episode closure/transition → mortuary/coronial/donation pathways where applicable.

name: Shared Object Integrity
pathways: create → reference → authorised update → propagate current state → detect/reject conflicting duplicate.

name: No Copy/Paste Clinical Architecture
pathways: source object → reference/link → role-specific presentation → authorised update to source.

name: Clinical Problem / Concern
pathways: concern identified → evidence → provisional problem → assessment → active problem → treatment/management linkage → monitoring → improving/stable/worsening → resolved/inactive → recurrence where applicable.

name: Symptom
pathways: symptom → onset → location/context → severity → pattern → associated features → assessment → intervention → reassessment → outcome.

name: Clinical Finding
pathways: observed/detected → recorded → interpreted → linked to assessment/problem/action where appropriate.

name: Intervention
pathways: intervention considered → planned → authorised where required → delivered/performed → response → reassessment → continued/modified/ceased.

name: Treatment Plan
pathways: treatment need → options → agreed/authorised plan → components → responsible services → implementation → monitoring → review → modification → completion/cessation.

name: Clinical Pathway / Protocol Instance
pathways: patient meets trigger/eligibility → pathway initiated → applicable steps → completed/skipped/not applicable/deferred states → deviations → escalation → completion/exit.
checklist required → individual check items due → check performed → evidence/response → exception → resolution/escalation → checklist completion.
assessment → recommendation → recipient → communicated → accepted/declined/modified → implementation requirement → implemented/not implemented → review.
requirement generated → pending → assigned → actioned OR deferred OR cancelled → outcome → closed.
requirement established → due date/time → upcoming → due → overdue → completed/ceased/rescheduled.

name: Clinical Checklist
rules: A checklist instance (e.g. medication round check, pre-procedure check) is a versioned template applied at a specific point in time; completing an item requires the specific worker's attribution.
An incomplete checklist is visibly distinguishable from a completed one and is never auto-completed by the passage of time or by navigating to the next screen.

name: Clinical Recommendation
pathways: proposed → communicated → acknowledged → accepted/declined/modified → resulting action separately created.

name: Pending Clinical Action
pathways: created → assigned → pending → in progress → completed/cancelled/unable to complete.

name: Due / Overdue State
pathways: future → due → overdue → escalated → completed/rescheduled/cancelled.

name: Recall
pathways: recall requirement → due interval/date → patient/service eligibility → invitation/contact → booking → attendance/action → outcome → next recall OR completion/exit.

name: Follow-Up Requirement
pathways: follow-up required → arrangement responsibility → referral/appointment/task linkage → scheduled → completed → outcome → further follow-up/closure.

name: Surveillance Plan
pathways: surveillance need → interval/trigger → required investigation/assessment → due → performed → result → review → continuation/modification/cessation.

name: Screening Episode
pathways: eligibility → invitation/offer → participation decision → screening action → result → review → communication → recall OR diagnostic escalation OR programme exit.

name: Immunisation Event
pathways: eligibility → consent → preparation → administration → observation → registry/reporting → next dose/follow-up.

name: Exposure Event
pathways: exposure identified → risk assessed → action required/not required → notification/testing/prophylaxis → follow-up → closed.

name: Infection Episode
pathways: suspected infection → evidence → site/source → organism where identified → susceptibility/resistance evidence → treatment → response → source control → complications → resolved/ongoing/recurrence.

name: Antimicrobial Course
pathways: infection/indication → antimicrobial decision → agent/order references → intended duration → microbiology linkage → review → escalation/de-escalation/change → completion/cessation → outcome.

name: Procedure Site / Laterality Verification
pathways: procedure planned → intended site/laterality → source evidence → patient/team verification where applicable → discrepancy → resolution → final verified state → procedure linkage.

name: Clinical Identity Verification
pathways: identity presented → identifiers checked → match confidence established → verified/unresolved/conflict → proceed or resolution workflow.

name: Clinical Readiness
pathways: readiness assessment required → prerequisites → completed/outstanding/not applicable → authorised assessment → ready/not ready/conditional → reassessment.

name: Contraindication
pathways: identified → evidence/source recorded → active → reviewed → remains/changes/resolved, with history.

name: Clinical Exception / Variance
pathways: expected state/action → variance → reason → clinical context → authorised decision → alternative action → monitoring/follow-up.

name: Refusal / Declined Care
pathways: care/intervention offered → relevant information/decision process → declined/refused → reason where offered/provided → immediate clinical implications → alternative plan → escalation where required → reassessment/re-offer where appropriate.

name: Cancellation
pathways: planned item → cancellation requested/triggered → reason → authorised cancellation → affected dependencies updated → patient/service notified → reschedule/close.

name: Did Not Attend / Unable to Complete Contact
pathways: expected contact → non-attendance/contact failure → attempt recorded → clinical risk assessed → retry/escalate/discharge according to applicable pathway.

name: Waiting List / Queue Position
pathways: accepted → prioritised → queued → reprioritised/reviewed → offered → scheduled → treated/removed/deferred, preserving history.

name: Clinical Priority / Triage
pathways: request/presentation → triage evidence → priority assigned → timeframe → reassessment → changed priority → service action.
incoming identity information → candidate match → matching evidence → confirmed match OR unresolved identity → merge/link correction process where authorised → provenance.
